Since I knew Mr. Karadzic as a God-fearing and honest person, I asked him about the destiny of those people. I asked him, 'Mr. President, what will be the lot of these people? Where are they being taken to? What is going to happen to them?'" I take it that those questions were questions you put to the president, Mr. Karadzic, when you met at Pale. Am I correct in so understanding?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the only thing I asked him. It was very short, he was nervous, and did not share any comments with me. I went out of the office and sat there with those fellows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. You pre-empted my question. So what was the -- Mr. Karadzic's answer to your question?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: He told me that I should mind my own business, that I should take care of my own. He said, Mind your own business, Puska. That's my nickname. And I said, Fine, and went out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bajagic. Unless --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellency, may I? One question only, a brief question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bajagic, what did you hear had happened in Kravica? Now, I'm not asking when you heard but what was it that you heard, what had happened? What was the information that reached you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Information spread to the effect that some of those prisoners had seized submachine-gun from one of the, I suppose, guards there and then the police executed them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, the questions about the hours and the various times, it doesn't mean that I arrived at 1800 hours. You see line 4.11, et cetera --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You're not giving evidence now. You will have ample opportunity for you to clarify these things. Are you done with Mr. Bajagic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me Mr. President. Just before the witness leaves, if there's any doubt, it seems clear to me, but I think it's very important that there be no doubt. If anyone wishes to put the question to him whether there was any discussion between him and Dr. Karadzic about what had happened at the Kravica warehouse this would be a good time otherwise I think the point is very clear that -- what the witness has answer about that but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mitchell, do you have any objection to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If they want to put the question, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you answer the question, Mr. Bajagic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear you. Could you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can answer. Was that the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what is the question I need to answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson. Could you ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Was there any discussion between you and Mr. Karadzic about what had happened at the Kravica warehouse when you saw him that late night in Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: No. No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That concludes your evidence, Mr. Bajagic. On behalf of the Chamber, I'd like to thank you for coming to The Hague to give it. Now you're free to go. But we'll rise all together. We'll continue tomorrow at 11.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 11th day of July, 2013, at 11.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.01 p.m.,
